newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on lower rates.

text.p: The Philippine peso fell prey to an outflow of arbitrage money triggered by lower domestic interest rates, traders said on Monday.
It closed at 26.341 in active trading from last Friday's close of 26.334, with the day's average at 26.339 from 26.331. Volume was still heavy at $269.10 million from $295.10 million.
The peso had skidded to a day-low of 26.343 in mid-day trade after the Treasury bill auction yielded a single-digit benchmark 91-day rate of 9.804 from 10.159 percent last week.
The decline in rates came after the Central Bank cut its key overnight borrowing rate last Friday to 10 from 10.25 percent.
Later, dollar inflows helped the peso gain some lost ground, traders said.
"Banks will be watching out for the Central Bank's next move. It might cut interest rates again," a dealer said, adding this will sharply weaken the peso if it happens.
Traders said the Central Bank stayed away from the market since the peso was still trading within its desired range. It gave a bid and offer rate for the dollar at 26.29/26.35.
